<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אלול_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518920191_theRebbe_834" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_9C_D7_95_D7_9C_meluket__BH_POST_1766518920191_theRebbe_834__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the fear in Elul is lower fear, stemming from G-d's greatness within creation, while the fear of Rosh Hashanah is higher fear, stemming from His transcendence above worlds, which can only be attained through a revelation from above.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by first explaining that the fear of Elul is lower fear, and the fear of Rosh Hashanah is higher fear.</t>
    <t s="2">For the difference between lower fear and higher fear is,</t>
    <t s="3">as explained in Tanya18</t>
    <t s="4">and in many places19,</t>
    <t s="5">that lower fear is from His greatness in the creation and bringing into being of the worlds.</t>
    <t s="6">For the self-nullification in this fear is the nullification of the sense of self (bitul hayesh).</t>
    <t s="7">And higher fear is from His greatness and sublimity that is above worlds,</t>
    <t s="8">for everything before Him is considered as nothing.</t>
    <t s="9">For the self-nullification in this fear is nullification of existence (bitul bimetziut).</t>
    <t s="10">And this is that in order to come to higher fear,</t>
    <t s="11">it is specifically through a revelation from above,</t>
    <t s="12">because what a person can attain through contemplation is the G-dliness that is relative to the worlds,</t>
    <t s="13">and in order for the sublimity of the Ein Sof that is above worlds to be felt by him, it is specifically through a revelation from above.</t>
    <t s="14">And this is what is stated20</t>
    <t s="15">"And the L-rd commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the L-rd,"</t>
    <t s="16">that in order to come to fear the L-rd,</t>
    <t s="17">higher fear21,</t>
    <t s="18">it is impossible to come to this through contemplation, but only through a revelation from above that is drawn down through the mitzvos22.</t>
    <t s="19">And this is that the fear of Elul is lower fear, and the fear of Rosh Hashanah is higher fear,</t>
    <t s="20">because in Elul,</t>
    <t s="21">when the king is in the field,</t>
    <t s="22">where being in the field, his greatness and sublimity are not felt23,</t>
    <t s="23">and the fear then is</t>
    <t s="24">(not from the aspect of revelation from above,</t>
    <t s="25">but rather)</t>
    <t s="26">through the service of man,</t>
    <t s="27">therefore,</t>
    <t s="28">the fear then is lower fear.</t>
    <t s="29">And on Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="30">when the king is in his palace of royalty,</t>
    <t s="31">when his sublimity is felt,</t>
    <t s="32">that he is elevated and separate from the people24,</t>
    <t s="33">for in the analogue, it is the revelation of the sublimity of the Ein Sof that is above worlds,</t>
    <t s="34">the fear on Rosh Hashanah is higher fear.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the shofar blast on Rosh Hashanah, being a mitzvah, brings about higher fear, whereas the shofar blast in Elul, not being a mitzvah, only brings lower fear, which serves as preparation for the higher fear.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that this that one must blow the shofar on Rosh Hashanah in order to come to higher fear,</t>
    <t s="2">even though at that time it is a time of the revelation of His kingship,</t>
    <t s="3">meaning that in the time of Rosh Hashanah, from its own essence, the sublimity of the Ein Sof that is above worlds shines in revelation,</t>
    <t s="4">this is,</t>
    <t s="5">because time is from the definitions of the world25,</t>
    <t s="6">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="7">the sublimity of the Ein Sof that is revealed on Rosh Hashanah from the aspect of the time of Rosh Hashanah is related to worlds,</t>
    <t s="8">and the revelation of the Ein Sof as it is holy and separate from worlds is primarily through the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="9">"Who sanctified us with His commandments"26.</t>
    <t s="10">And since the shofar blast on Rosh Hashanah is a mitzvah,</t>
    <t s="11">the fear and trembling from the sound of the shofar of Rosh Hashanah is fear and nullification to the utmost,</t>
    <t s="12">higher fear.</t>
    <t s="13">And based on this, there is further explanation in this, that the fear that comes from the sound of the shofar of Elul is</t>
    <t s="14">(only)</t>
    <t s="15">lower fear,</t>
    <t s="16">because this that the sound of the shofar of Rosh Hashanah brings about such an immense fear,</t>
    <t s="17">nullification of existence</t>
    <t s="18">(higher fear),</t>
    <t s="19">is from the aspect of the mitzvah of shofar blast,</t>
    <t s="20">and since the shofar blast in Elul is not a mitzvah</t>
    <t s="21">(and we do not recite the blessing "Who sanctified us with His commandments" over it),</t>
    <t s="22">therefore,</t>
    <t s="23">the fear</t>
    <t s="24">(and nullification)</t>
    <t s="25">that comes from the sound of the shofar of Elul is</t>
    <t s="26">(only)</t>
    <t s="27">nullification of the sense of self,</t>
    <t s="28">lower fear.</t>
    <t s="29">However, nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="30">this fear is an introduction and preparation for the higher fear of Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="31">because in order to come to higher fear, one must first have lower fear</t>
    <t s="32">(as mentioned above in the maamar).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that to ascend from lower fear to higher fear, love must first be aroused, as illustrated by the king in the field who receives everyone with a pleasant countenance, corresponding to the two levels of love, leading to the higher fear in the palace.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is known27</t>
    <t s="2">that in order to come from lower fear to higher fear, one must first have love.</t>
    <t s="3">For the order of service is: fear, love, love, and fear.</t>
    <t s="4">Fear</t>
    <t s="5">(the first)</t>
    <t s="6">is lower fear,</t>
    <t s="7">and afterwards, two levels in love,</t>
    <t s="8">lower love (ahava zuta) and great love (ahava rabbah),</t>
    <t s="9">and afterwards, fear,</t>
    <t s="10">higher fear.</t>
    <t s="11">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="12">that this that from the lower fear of Elul one comes to the higher fear of Rosh Hashanah is through the prior introduction of love.</t>
    <t s="13">And this can be explained based on what is stated in Likkutei Torah, that when the king is in the field, he receives everyone with a pleasant countenance and shows a smiling face to all,</t>
    <t s="14">for a pleasant countenance and a smiling face are the matter of love,</t>
    <t s="15">and by the king receiving everyone with a pleasant countenance,</t>
    <t s="16">and especially by showing a smiling face to all,</t>
    <t s="17">this arouses in them</t>
    <t s="18">(as in water, face to face28)</t>
    <t s="19">love for the king.</t>
    <t s="20">And based on this, it can be said,</t>
    <t s="21">that in the details of the analogy in Likkutei Torah, the four aforementioned matters are hinted at.</t>
    <t s="22">For this that they go out to greet the king to receive his face,</t>
    <t s="23">pertains to lower fear.</t>
    <t s="24">And afterwards,</t>
    <t s="25">the king receives them with a pleasant countenance and shows them a smiling face – the two levels of love</t>
    <t s="26">(pleasant countenance – lower love,</t>
    <t s="27">and smiling face – great love),</t>
    <t s="28">and afterwards comes the matter of when he enters his palace of royalty – higher fear.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
